about.temperature: Air temperature measured in the shade, 2 metres above the ground. Past hours are drawn faded, the hours ahead bright; slide your finger over the chart to read any hour exactly.
about.feels: Feels-like temperature is how the air feels to your body. Wind carries heat away and makes it feel colder, while high humidity makes warm air feel muggier. The dashed line is the actual temperature.
about.wind: Wind speed is the average speed measured 10 metres above the ground. Gusts are short bursts of a few seconds and are usually well above the average. The arrows show where the wind is blowing.
about.beaufort: The Beaufort scale rates the strength of the wind from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force). Each level describes how the wind affects its surroundings. The chosen day's level is highlighted.
about.illumination: Illumination is how much of the side of the Moon facing Earth is lit by the Sun: 100% at full moon, 0% at new moon. The Moon completes a cycle every 29.5 days; scroll the timeline to see the phase on any day.
about.sun: First light is when the sky starts to brighten, with the Sun 6° below the horizon; last light is when evening twilight ends. Solar noon is when the Sun is highest in the sky.
about.uv: The UV index is the strength of the Sun's ultraviolet rays. From 3 up, protection is advised; from 6 up, stay in the shade around midday. UV can be high even under clouds.
about.humidity: Relative humidity is how much water vapour the air holds compared with the most it could hold. High humidity makes warm weather feel muggy and cold weather feel damp and chillier.
about.dewPoint: The dew point is the temperature at which the air would have to cool for its water vapour to condense. A dew point above 16° feels muggy; below 10° feels dry and comfortable.
about.visibility: Visibility is how far away you can clearly see objects. Fog, mist, rain and snow reduce it. More than 10 km means a clear day.
about.pressure: Atmospheric pressure adjusted to sea level. Falling pressure often means clouds and precipitation are on the way; rising pressure points to calmer, clearer weather.
